output_json.patch_notes: Commandline.java: added getLiteralExecutable() (raw executable, no shell quoting) and changed getCommandline()/Marker.getPosition()/verifyShellState() to use it instead of the shell-mutated getExecutable(); changed execute() to run Runtime.exec(getCommandline(), environment, workingDir) for both the with- and without-workingDir branches instead of Runtime.exec(getShellCommandline(), ...), i.e. processes are launched directly as an argv array without ever invoking /bin/sh or cmd.exe on attacker-controlled content. Shell.java: added unconditionallyQuote flag + setUnconditionalQuoting(), extracted quoteOneItem() (always calls StringUtils.quoteAndEscape with the configured quote delimiter/escape chars), and switched getRawCommandLine()/getShellCommandLine() to build from getOriginalExecutable() through quoteOneItem() rather than the previous conditional escaping path. BourneShell.java: executable quote delimiter changed from '\"' to '\'' (double quotes don't block $()/backtick expansion in POSIX shells, single quotes do), setUnconditionalQuoting(true), and unifyQuotes()/getQuotingTriggerChars() replaced by quoteOneItem() which unconditionally wraps every executable/argument/working-directory token in single quotes and escapes embedded single quotes via the standard '"'"' technique — no more "already looks quoted, pass through unescaped" shortcut. Test files updated to match the new (always-quoted) shell command-line output, matching the real upstream 3.0.16 fix, plus a new testPathWithShellExpansionStrings regression test for an executable path containing '$'.
output_json.risk_notes: This mirrors the exact upstream plexus-utils 3.0.15→3.0.16 security fix, so behavior changes are expected and scoped: getShellCommandline()/toString() output is now always fully single-quoted (previously unquoted/selectively quoted) — any caller doing string-matching on that exact format (rather than executing it) could see different literal output, though it remains valid shell syntax. The bigger behavioral change is that Commandline.execute() no longer spawns an intermediate shell at all (direct exec of the argv array) — this removes shell features like variable expansion, globbing, and `&&`/`;` chaining from execute() for legitimate callers who relied on shell semantics; those callers should use getShellCommandline() explicitly with their own shell if such semantics are truly required. Full existing test suite (284 tests) passes unchanged in behaviorally-neutral cases; the intentionally-updated assertions were verified against the actual upstream 3.0.16 release to confirm correctness rather than guessed.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-078 OS command injection in plexus-utils' Commandline/Shell command-line construction (this project is plexus-utils 3.0.15, the version vulnerable to CVE-2017-1000487 / GHSA-8vhq-qq4p-grq3). Root cause: (1) Commandline.execute() built one big string via Shell.getShellCommandLine() and ran it through `/bin/sh -c <string>`, so attacker-controlled executable/argument values containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `` ` ``, `$()`, etc.) were interpreted by the shell; and (2) BourneShell quoted the executable with double quotes and used a conditional/"already looks quoted" escaping shortcut in Shell.getRawCommandLine, neither of which reliably neutralizes shell metacharacters (double quotes still allow `$()`/backtick expansion, and the conditional shortcut could be bypassed). Applied the same fix upstream shipped in plexus-utils 3.0.16: Commandline.execute() now calls Runtime.exec(getCommandline(), env, workingDir) — a direct argv exec with no intermediate shell — for both overloads (previously both called getShellCommandline()). Shell/BourneShell now always single-quote and unconditionally escape the executable and every argument (new Shell.quoteOneItem()/unconditionallyQuote, BourneShell executable quote delimiter changed from `"` to `'`, unifyQuotes replaced with an unconditional `'...'` wrap that escapes embedded quotes via the standard `'"'"'` POSIX technique). getShellCommandline() (retained for remote-execution/display use cases) now always produces a safely quoted string too. Verified with a manual PoV: an executable string containing `; touch /tmp/pwned #` and arguments containing `$(...)`/backticks no longer create the marker file when executed via Commandline.execute(), and getShellCommandline() renders them fully single-quoted.
